purpose: Reviewed public program architecture used as bounded evidence input to the generic Monitor technical-decomposition workflow. These records contain only high-level publicly released architecture; they are not controlled drawings, supplier assertions, awards, or proof of BTX participation.

sources.title: Javelin Joint Venture and Tata Advanced Systems Signs Agreement for Missile Co-Production in India
sources.passage: The Javelin Joint Venture and Tata Advanced Systems entered a memorandum of understanding to explore final assembly and integration of the Javelin All Up Round and component production in India. The release states that multiyear sub-assembly kits would be produced at Lockheed Martin's Troy, Alabama facility and guidance electronics units at Raytheon's Tucson, Arizona facility for shipment to India.

sources.title: Through Lockheed and Raytheon Collaboration, The West Point Museum Unveils Javelin Exhibit
sources.passage: The U.S. Army article describes the public exhibit as including a Command Launch Unit, Launch Tube Assembly, and a full-sized replica of the Javelin missile.

sources.title: TC 3-22.37 Javelin—Close Combat Missile System, Medium
sources.passage: The public Army training circular identifies the Javelin missile sections as guidance, warhead, mid-body, propulsion, and control actuator. The same public system description identifies the Battery Coolant Unit as part of the round equipment. Only this high-level published architecture is retained.

sources.title: Javelin Weapon System
sources.passage: RTX describes Javelin as an anti-tank guided munition made by the Javelin Joint Venture between Raytheon and Lockheed Martin and identifies the Command Launch Unit as the system sight and launcher context.
